answerlines: Muhammad [accept alternate versions of his name like Mohamed, Muhammud, etc.]

clues.text: Scholars debate whether Satan occupied this figure’s tongue when they praised Lāt, Uzzá, and Manāt as “exalted cranes.”
This man’s last action on his deathbed was to bequeath seven coins to his wife.
The year this man was born is referred to as the Year of the Elephant.
This figure’s first wife, Khadīja, was a Quraysh merchant who advised him after an event he experienced in the Cave of Hira.
He employed clever defense tactics at the Battle of the Ditch.
The Year of Sorrow in this man’s life included the death of his wife Khadijah; three years later, he led the Hijra, a migration from his hometown to Medina.
This figure’s sayings are collected in the hadiths.
During the Hijra, this figure fled to Medina after being persecuted for preaching monotheism.
This religious figure led his followers to Medina from his home city, Mecca.
Jibril revealed the Qur'an to what figure, who is considered in Islam to be the final prophet of Allah?
In this religion, the Daena appears to souls who were good in life, who are then guided to the House of Song.
A prophecy in this religion claims that a comet will turn metal into a river that purifies men.
Children are initiated into this religion by receiving the sudreh undershirt and kusti thread.
A heresy among members of this religion was based on a personification of time named Zurvan.
Members of this religion are judged at the Chinvat Bridge after death.
An important concept in this religion is the contrast between asha and druj, or truth and lies.
Due to its belief in the sacredness of the elements, this religion exposes corpses on the Towers of Silence.
Followers must choose between druj and asha, and scripture in this religion includes the Vendidad and Gathas, both contained within the Avesta.
The evil spirit Ahriman fights this religion’s creator god, Ahura Mazda.
Name this ancient Persian religion founded by its namesake prophet.

answerlines: Taoism [or Daoism; accept Zhengyi Taoism or Tianshi Taoism; accept "What is Taoism?" or Hsien Taoism or contemplative Taoism or purposive Taoism]

clues.text: This religion is described as developing after "contemplative" and "purposive" counterparts in a paper by Herrlee Creel titled "What is?"; that paper references a supernatural state sought by its priests by prepending its name with hsien ("shyen").
In traditional depictions of the “vinegar tasters”, the founder of this philosophy is depicted as having a happy expression, symbolizing this movement’s generally positive view of life.
Writings in this belief system compare the naming of a concept to cutting an uncarved block of wood.
In an allegory, its founder blamed his mind for the sour taste of vinegar.
Ziran, or naturalness, is a concept associated with this belief system.
A concept from this religion in which things tend to happen by themselves is known as ziran.
The Eight Immortals are revered in this religion.
A scholar who dreamt that he was a dreaming butterfly adhered to this belief system, which stresses acting without action, or wu wei.
Name this philosophically entrenched Chinese religion that espouses wu wei and the teachings of Laozi.
Name this religion, whose principal text, the Tao Te Ching, was written by Lao Tzu.
